latestVersion.description:
Jedi chooses the wrong overload when the parameter is annotated with `type[...]`. With `get_obj(input: type[Foo]) -> FooBuilder` and `get_obj(input: type[Bar]) -> BarBuilder`, when typing `get_obj(Foo).` Jedi suggests methods of both `FooBuilder` and `BarBuilder`, while only `FooBuilder` should be suggested. A `type[X]` parameter accepts class `X` and its subclasses, not instances. Annotation `type`, `Type` or `type[Any]` accepts all classes. With `type[T]` where `T` is TypeVar, the class must satisfy the bounds or one of the constraints of `T`; If `T` has no bounds and no constraints, then all classes are accepted. The `Optional[X]` parameter takes `None` and any value that `X` takes. With annotation containers like `list[X]` or `dict[K, V]`, every element of the argument must be accepted by the corresponding annotation; With dict, both key and value must be accepted.

Jedi should choose overload as a type checker: the first overload where every invocation argument (either by position or by name) matches the annotation will be used, and only if no overload matches will combine the results of all overloads. If an argument passed by position or by name can have multiple types (e.g. Union), the annotation must accept all of those types. When parameters receive arguments via `*args` or `**kwargs`, annotations describing each argument are aggregated; Arguments unpacked from a tuple, list, or dict at the call are also counted, including dicts created by a `dict(...)` call in any call form that `dict` supports. These rules also apply when an overloaded function is called via `functools.partial`. If `*args` or `**kwargs` receives no arguments, the overload still matches.

+"""
+Choosing the overload of a function from the arguments of a call.
+"""
+
+from textwrap import dedent
+
+import pytest
+
+HEADER = """\
+from typing import overload, Any, Type, TypeVar, Union
+
+class A: pass
+class B(A): pass
+class C: pass
+class RA: pass
+class RB: pass
+class RC: pass
+"""
+
+
+def overloads(*annotations):
+    code = ''
+    for annotation, result in zip(annotations, ('RA', 'RB', 'RC')):
+        code += '@overload\ndef f(x: %s) -> %s: ...\n' % (annotation, result)
+    return code + 'def f(x): ...\n'
+
+
+def infer_result(Script, code):
+    code = HEADER + dedent(code).strip('\n')
+    lines = code.splitlines()
+    return sorted(d.name for d in Script(code).infer(len(lines), len(lines[-1])))
+
+
+def check(Script, annotations, call, expected, prefix=''):
+    code = prefix + overloads(*annotations) + call
+    assert infer_result(Script, code) == expected, (annotations, call)
+
+
+def test_issue_example(Script):
+    code = dedent('''\
+        from typing import overload
+
+        class Foo: pass
+
+        class FooBuilder:
+            def func_foo(self): pass
+
+        class Bar: pass
+
+        class BarBuilder:
+            def func_bar(self): pass
+
+        @overload
+        def get_obj(input: type[Foo]) -> FooBuilder: ...
+        @overload
+        def get_obj(input: type[Bar]) -> BarBuilder: ...
+        def get_obj(input: type): pass
+
+        builder = get_obj(Foo)
+        builder.''')
+    names = [c.name for c in Script(code).complete()]
+    assert 'func_foo' in names
+    assert 'func_bar' not in names
+
+    code = code.replace('get_obj(Foo)', 'get_obj(Bar)')
+    names = [c.name for c in Script(code).complete()]
+    assert 'func_bar' in names
+    assert 'func_foo' not in names
+

Expand the tests and implementation around unpacking. Add mixed-type cases where an incompatible annotated-container member arrives through `*`, where a dict-literal member arrives through `**`, and where `dict(...)` consumes a generator of pairs. Also make call-time `*` expansion recursively account for starred members inside list and tuple literals; the current strict matcher either drops those members or turns them into unknown values. Avoid silently discarding still-visible dict entries when the recursion guard is reached, even if the guard itself remains.

output.taskSummary: The task is to make Jedi choose an overloaded function’s return type from the call’s inferred argument types. A candidate overload matches only when all supplied arguments fit their annotations; the first matching overload wins, and if none matches, results from all overloads are combined. The prompt also specifies type[X]/TypeVar behavior, Optional, generic containers, union-valued arguments, variadic and unpacked arguments, dict(...) construction, and functools.partial. The new tests exercise those behaviors through inferred return-type names and code completion.

reviews.feedback:
Tests: T4: All 62 new tests pass despite incorrect handling of nested starred arguments, custom mapping inputs to dict(), empty dictionary comprehensions, forward-referenced TypeVar bounds, and uncertain partial keywords. These are material gaps in the requested argument-matching behavior. Add discriminating cases for these forms, conditional dictionary overwrites, and fixed versus variable-length tuples.

Solution & Code: S1/S2: The following material issues remain:

1. TypeVar.annotation_accepts in gradual/type_var.py treats quoted bounds and constraints as string values instead of resolving their referenced types. With T = TypeVar("T", bound="A"), type[T] rejects B where B subclasses A, producing fallback results. Resolve forward references before checking compatibility.

2. The variadic argument path still drops nested starred contents. With unrelated A and C, f(*[A, *[C]]) selects an A-only overload instead of rejecting both homogeneous alternatives; f(*[*[C]]) behaves as though no arguments were supplied. Apply complete sequence expansion when matching invocation arguments.

3. Generic mapping extraction in arguments.py assumes values()/iteration rather than supporting dict’s keys()/__getitem__ protocol. A mapping whose keys() returns ["p"] and whose __getitem__ returns C causes f(**dict(mapping)) to combine overloads instead of selecting the C overload. Separately, _value_entries treats a proven-empty comprehension as unknown: f(**{k: C for k in []}) combines overloads instead of selecting the first empty-compatible overload. Preserve both mapping contents and known emptiness.

4. _dict_literal_pairs and _dict_call_pairs discard known key identities when merging alternative mappings. Consequently, dict({"p": A} if condition else {}, p=C) retains the overwritten A possibility and rejects dict[str, type[C]], although its final value is always C. Preserve keys so later entries correctly replace earlier alternatives.

5. iterate_elements marks nonliteral tuple summaries as having an exact length. An argument annotated tuple[int, ...] therefore selects an earlier tuple[int] overload, even though its length is unknown. Track cardinality separately from the iterator’s representative element types.

6. MergedPartialArguments.unpack loses keyword uncertainty. partial(f, **{k1: A})(**{k2: C}), with arbitrary string keys, treats the unknown keys as identical and selects a C-only overload even when both values may remain. Merging two possibly absent bindings also incorrectly makes the parameter guaranteed present. Preserve uncertain key identity and presence.

7. The new protocol matcher introduces a verified regression: _member_compatible accepts an integer attribute in place of a required method and accepts methods with additional required parameters. These cases correctly selected the object fallback on BASE but select the protocol overload on SOLVED. Validate member callability and the complete compatible signature.

8. The repository’s configured zuban check passes on BASE but fails on SOLVED with four new errors: arguments.py lines 594, 596, and 634, and gradual/base.py line 57. Correct the heterogeneous lazy-value collection types so the required code-quality check passes.
